title: Hard to Believe
subject: fun-facts
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Eight answers that sound made up. All eight check out.
completionMessage: Every square filled, every fact still standing.

entries.explanation: Its droppings really are cubic; the corners form inside the intestine, not at the exit.
entries.sourceNotes: Reported by P. Yang and colleagues in Soft Matter (2021), which traced the shape to uneven stiffness in the intestinal wall.

entries.explanation: Two branchial hearts serve the gills, one systemic heart serves the body; the copper-based pigment haemocyanin makes the blood blue.
entries.sourceNotes: Standard cephalopod physiology; see Encyclopaedia Britannica, entry on octopus.

entries.explanation: Flying squirrels glide; these are the only mammals that flap.

entries.clue: Name for the dot over an i
entries.explanation: The word survives mainly in the phrase "to a jot and a ___".
entries.sourceNotes: Oxford English Dictionary gives the sense "the dot over the letter i".

entries.clue: River heavyweight whose sweat runs red
entries.explanation: The reddish secretion is not blood but hipposudoric acid, which screens sunlight and discourages bacteria.
entries.sourceNotes: Described by Saikawa and colleagues in Nature (2004), "Pigment chemistry: the red sweat of the hippopotamus".

entries.explanation: Sealed and dry, it keeps almost indefinitely — see the fact cards.
Shark-like fish appear in the fossil record tens of millions of years before the first forests.
entries.sourceNotes: Natural History Museum (London), shark evolution pages.

entries.clue: Himalayan legend unmasked by bear DNA
entries.explanation: Museum and monastery samples collected as evidence turned out to be bear — mostly Himalayan brown and Asian black bear.
entries.sourceNotes: Lindqvist and colleagues, Proceedings of the Royal Society B (2017), on the genetic identity of purported yeti samples.

factCards.text: Honey does not spoil. Its very low water content and natural acidity leave microbes nothing to grow on, so a sealed jar keeps for years without refrigeration.
factCards.sourceTitle: National Honey Board — Honey Storage and Shelf Life

factCards.text: Wombats are the only known animals to produce cube-shaped faeces. Researchers found the corners are moulded by stretchier and stiffer patches in the intestinal wall, not by a square exit.
factCards.sourceTitle: Soft Matter (2021) — study on the formation of cube-shaped wombat faeces

factCards.text: Sharks are older than trees. Shark-like fish appear in the fossil record around 420 million years ago, while the earliest forests date to roughly 385 million years ago.
